thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Nikkei Tumbles, China Stocks Find Strength, Following Tech Losses On Wall Street

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Nikkei Tumbles, China Stocks Find Strength, Following Tech Losses On Wall Street
text:
By Dow Jones Newswires
Nikkei down 2%; Apple component suppliers hit hard
Asian stock markets saw volatile trading Tuesday following Monday's rout, led by tech stocks, on Wall Street.
Every sector in Japan's stock market turned lower as the Nikkei dropped more than 2%. Investors were quick to react to the U.S. losses, especially among suppliers linked to Apple's (AAPL) iPhone. TDK (6762.TO) and Murata (6981.TO) were down about 7% and 5%, respectively. Meanwhile, SoftBank (9984.TO) rose 2%, making up an early 4% loss, following its after-the-bell update on the planned IPO for its Japanese mobile unit. Japanese auto companies also fell after reports that the Trump administration is planning tariffs on auto imports, with Toyota (7203.TO) and Honda (HMC) down over 2% each.
Bucking an earlier sharper drop, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 0.2%, with energy stocks weak given oil's sharp reversal, with CNOOC (0883.HK) falling 4%.
Mainland China stocks fared better, with the Shanghai Composite managing a gain of nearly 2% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite about flat. Still, iPhone component suppliers Secote Precision (603283.SH) and Luxshare (002475.SZ) were down some 2% each.
Benchmark indexes in South Korea and Taiwan dropped roughly 0.5% each, weighed down by tech names. Samsung (005930.SE) fell almost 2% and SK Hynix (000660.SE) plummeted 3.6% while Taiwan Semiconductor (2330.TW) was off 1.7%.
Australia's ASX 200 closed down 0.18%, as energy and financial names dropped, and New Zealand stocks slipped about 1%.
